text.p: PRAVDA - Jan Slota, Chairman of the nationalist junior member of the ruling coalition, the Slovak National Party (SNS), is expected to meet the Austrian far-right leader Joerg Haider in May this year. Slota should also meet the extreme- right French National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen during his visit to Slovakia, expected by the end of May.

- Slovakia is negotiating with Russia on purchase of six military helicopters Ka-50, the so-called Black Sharks. According to Russian military sources, the contract should be signed by the end of this month.
NARODNA OBRODA - The International Court of Justice in The Hague opens on Monday a law suit between Hungary and Slovakia over the controversial Gabcikovo dam on the River Danube.
- Sales of agricultural products totalled some 33.8 billion crowns in 1996, an increase of 6.7 percent over the previous year.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The only Slovak producer of matches, Zapalkaren Banska Bystrica, said dumped imports from Poland and the Baltic countries could soon destroy domestic production. Zapalkarena has asked the economics ministry to impose limits on import of matches.
- Employees of the state-run postal monopoly Slovenska Posta, demand an increase of wages of at least six percent this year, but say the pay rise should not include the company's management.

SME - The Slovak Jewish community expects a final agreement with the Czech finance ministry on return of the gold and precious stones that belonged to Slovak Jews before the Holocaust, currently held by the Czech National Bank, within two to three months.

- Bela Bugar, leader of the opposition Hungarian Christian Democratic Movement (MKDH), said dismissal of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's governemnt should not neccessarily lead to early elections. Meciar has repeatedly said he plans to link the vote on a law barring bank sell-off with a no-confidence vote againts his cabinet.
